hints.content:
For a function to be continuous over an entire interval, it has to be continuous on every point in that interval.

Graphically, this is roughly the same as being able to draw the graph of the function on that interval without lifting the pencil.

![Function f is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 8. The graph consists of 1 curve. The curve starts at about (negative 8, 3), moves upward to about (negative 7, 6), moves downward then upward to about (negative 6, 6), moves downward through an open circle at (negative 5, 3) to about (negative 2, negative 7), moves upward to about (4, 1.5), moves downward to (5, 1), moves upward to (6, 4), moves downward then upward to (7, 4), moves downward, and ends at (8, 1).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/f5501a7a26f7102ae2774fd525de074e2af7fe8f)

$f$ appears to be continuous on the interval $[2,7]$.

$f$ appears to be continuous on the interval $[-4,0]$.
In conclusion, $f$ is continuous over both $[2,7]$ and $[-4,0]$.
